name: Statin use versus non-use and venous thromboembolism; capacity-only specification; evidence cutoff 2008-11-19

metadata.benchmark: JUPITER randomized rosuvastatin trial; VTE outcome reported in 2009. Benchmark only; not an evidence cell.
metadata.cutoff_rationale: The JUPITER trial's first publication was 2008-11-20 (primary trial paper). The VTE-specific secondary-outcome article appeared online 2009-03-29. The stricter first-trial-publication cutoff is used: only studies published before 2008-11-20 are eligible.
metadata.placeholder_rule: Every cell estimate is 1.0 on the ratio scale and every SE is 0.1 on the log scale. These are computational placeholders, not empirical estimates.
metadata.selection_rule: Candidate 1 qualifies first: pre-cutoff observational evidence includes both a population-based retrospective cohort and a matched case-control design. Later candidates are not evaluated because the ordered rule stops at the first qualifying candidate.

cells.design: population-based retrospective follow-up cohort; current/recent statin use versus normolipidaemic non-use; idiopathic VTE
cells.source: Yang CC, Jick SS, Jick H. Statins and the risk of idiopathic venous thromboembolism. Br J Clin Pharmacol. 2002;53(1):101-105. DOI: 10.1046/j.0306-5251.2001.01523.x. Primary report; cohort/follow-up estimate.

cells.design: hospital-based matched case-control study; statin use versus non-use; composite VTE
cells.source: Lacut K, Oger E, Le Gal G, et al. Statins but not fibrates are associated with a reduced risk of venous thromboembolism: a hospital-based case-control study. Fundam Clin Pharmacol. 2004;18(4):477-482. DOI: 10.1111/j.1472-8206.2004.00252.x. PubMed PMID: 15312155; primary abstract.

assumptions.name: H_HEALTHY_USER_BIAS_TOWARD_LOWER_RISK
assumptions.source: Brookhart MA, Patrick AR, Dormuth C, et al. Adherence to lipid-lowering therapy and the use of preventive health services: an investigation of the healthy user effect. Am J Epidemiol. 2007;166(3):348-354. DOI: 10.1093/aje/kwm070. Statin users/adherers were more likely to use preventive health services despite adjustment, supporting a plausible negative (protective) direction for healthy-user/adherer bias. This is directional only; no VTE-specific bias magnitude is asserted.
